body:
### Description

This PR sits on top of #14745 in the refreshable-token stack. Testing refresh behavior by hand is awkward because GitHub issues expiring access tokens with a lifetime of 8 hours and refresh tokens with a lifetime of 6 months, so there is no practical way to wait for a real expiry. Until now the stack relied on ad hoc `os.Getenv` hacks (`GH_AT_EXPIRES_IN`, `GH_RT_EXPIRES_IN`, and `GH_DEBUG_REFRESH_TOKEN`) that were compiled into every build, including release binaries.

This replaces those hacks with a small `internal/debug` package. `debug.Config()` returns a `debug.DebugConfig` value whose fields are `Option` values, one per override, read from the environment only when gh is built with the `ghdebug` build tag. An unset override is `None`, so an explicit zero or `false` is still distinguishable from no override. The tag is prefixed with `gh` so it cannot collide with a generic `debug` tag that a dependency or another tool might use. In a regular build the package compiles to a stub that always returns an empty `DebugConfig` with every override `None`, so the overrides do not exist in released binaries and cannot be switched on by setting an environment variable. The parsing itself lives in an unexported, untagged `configFromEnv`, so the regular test run covers it on every OS; only the `ghdebug` implementation of `Config` calls it, and the linker drops it from regular builds.

The overrides, all prefixed `GH_INTERNAL_` to make it clear they are not a supported interface:

- `GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN`: access token lifetime in seconds, measured from when the token was issued. With `1`, any stored access token is already treated as expired, so the next use triggers a refresh.
- `GH_INTERNAL_RT_EXPIRES_IN`: refresh token lifetime in seconds, measured the same way. When it is exceeded, gh behaves as if the server rejected the refresh token: it clears the stored credential and asks the user to run `gh auth login`.
- `GH_INTERNAL_DEBUG_REFRESH_TOKEN`: a boolean. By default the refresh exchange is logged as head lines only under `GH_DEBUG=api`; set it to `true` to log the full refresh request and response.

An invalid value panics in a debug build, so a typo cannot silently fall back to the real lifetime.

To make getting a debug binary easy, there is a new `make debug` target. It does the same as `make` but passes the `ghdebug` build tag, producing `bin/gh` with the overrides enabled. The build script now also compares the build tags embedded in an existing `bin/gh` with `GO_BUILDTAGS`, so switching between `make` and `make debug` always rebuilds, while repeating the same one still skips an up to date binary. CI also builds `./cmd/gh` with `-tags=ghdebug` on the Ubuntu runner, so the debug variant cannot silently stop compiling.

A debug binary identifies itself in its version output, so it is easy to tell which kind of binary you are running:

```
$ bin/gh version
gh version 2.100.0-180-g76df8f52a (2026-10-19) [debug build]
```

The two guided e2e scripts (`script/refreshable-token-e2e.sh` and `script/refreshable-token-gitcredential-e2e.sh`) now use the `GH_INTERNAL_` names, check `gh version` for the `[debug build]` marker and refuse to run against a regular binary, and point at `make debug`. Their own settings are renamed to match: `GH_BIN`, `GH_E2E_HOST`, and `GH_E2E_ALLOW_VSCODE` become `GH_INTERNAL_E2E_BIN`, `GH_INTERNAL_E2E_HOST`, and `GH_INTERNAL_E2E_ALLOW_VSCODE`.

The main e2e script also checks more of the behavior from earlier PRs in the stack. Every `gh auth token` step that prints a stored expiring token now asserts that the expiry warning appears on stderr, and the steps that print a non-expiring token (such as one from `GH_TOKEN`) assert that it does not. There is also a new `gh auth refresh` step without `--expiring`, next to the existing one with it, and both assert that gh asked for and received an expiring refreshable token.

#### Trying it out

Build a debug binary and log in with an expiring token:

```sh
make debug
bin/gh auth login --expiring
```

Then force the access token to count as expired and make any API call with `GH_DEBUG=api`:

```sh
GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN=1 GH_DEBUG=api bin/gh api user --jq .login
```

A refresh shows up in stderr as a request to the OAuth token endpoint, before the `api/user` request:

```
* Request to https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
```

Running the same command without `GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN` shows no such line, because the freshly refreshed token is still valid. `bin/gh auth status` also shows the new expiry time. Add `GH_INTERNAL_DEBUG_REFRESH_TOKEN=true` to see the full refresh exchange instead of just its head lines.

To see what happens when the refresh token itself has expired (this logs you out of the host in gh):

```sh
GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN=1 GH_INTERNAL_RT_EXPIRES_IN=1 bin/gh api user
```

For a guided walkthrough of every scenario, run `script/refreshable-token-e2e.sh` or `script/refreshable-token-gitcredential-e2e.sh` after `make debug`.

### How did you test this change?

I ran `make` and `make debug` and compared the two binaries. `bin/gh version` printed `gh version 2.100.0-180-g76df8f52a (2026-10-19)` for the regular build and the same line with a trailing `[debug build]` for the debug build, and `gh --version` matched in both cases. `go version -m bin/gh` reported `-tags=ghdebug` for the debug build. I also ran `make debug`, `make`, `make`, `make debug`, `make debug` in sequence: every switch between the two rebuilt with the right tags, and every repeat reported `bin/gh` as up to date. I also built regular and `ghdebug` binaries for linux/amd64, windows/amd64, windows/arm64, darwin/amd64, and darwin/arm64: no regular build contains any `GH_INTERNAL_` string or the `configFromEnv` and `lifetimeFromEnv` symbols, while every `ghdebug` build contains all of them.

I ran `script/refreshable-token-e2e.sh` against the debug binary and all scenarios passed, including the new `gh auth token` warning checks and both `gh auth refresh` steps, with and without `--expiring`.

I ran `script/refreshable-token-gitcredential-e2e.sh` against the debug binary in an Ubuntu 25.10 container with git 2.51.0, so the git 2.46+ `authtype` credential capability path was exercised, and all scenarios passed.

### Key points

- The overrides are compiled out rather than hidden behind an undocumented variable, so there is no way to enable them in a release build. For the same reason the debug check is a version marker rather than something like a `GH_INTERNAL_IS_DEBUG` variable: a release binary has no code that reads `GH_INTERNAL_*` variables, so it could not respond to one without adding such code to release builds.
- The lifetime overrides are measured from issuance, not from now. `GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN=3600` therefore means "pretend the token was issued with a one hour lifetime", which keeps the behavior consistent across repeated invocations.
- The simulated refresh token expiry follows the same path as a real server rejection, including only clearing the stored credential when the refresh lock is held.
- `make debug` writes to the same `bin/gh` as `make`, so the two builds replace each other rather than coexisting.

### Notes for reviewers

Start with `internal/debug/config.go` (the `DebugConfig` type and the untagged `configFromEnv` parser) and its two build-tagged implementations (`config_enabled.go` and `config_disabled.go`, which pick what `Config` returns and define `debug.Enabled`), then `pkg/cmd/version/version.go` for the version marker, then the call sites in `internal/config/refreshable.go` (`accessTokenNeedsRefresh` and `simulateRefreshTokenExpired`) and `pkg/cmd/factory/default.go` (`tokenRefresherHttpClientFunc`). In the scripts, the debug check is `require_gh`, and apart from the renames the only new logic is the `auth token` warning and `auth refresh` assertions in `script/refreshable-token-e2e.sh`.

commits.messageBody:
Add an internal/debug package that exposes Config, which returns a
DebugConfig holding internal debugging overrides as Option values, and
Enabled, which reports whether gh was built with the ghdebug build tag.
In ghdebug builds Config reads GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN and
GH_INTERNAL_RT_EXPIRES_IN as token lifetimes in seconds and
GH_INTERNAL_DEBUG_REFRESH_TOKEN as a boolean, leaves unset overrides as
None, and panics on invalid values. In regular builds every override is
always None, so the overrides cannot be enabled in released binaries.
The tag is prefixed with gh to avoid colliding with a generic debug tag.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.messageBody:
Add "make debug", which builds bin/gh like "make" but with the ghdebug
build tag so the internal debug overrides are available. It removes
bin/gh first because script/build skips rebuilding when no source file
has changed.

when gh is built with the ghdebug build tag, so a debug binary is easy

commits.messageBody:
Replace the ad hoc os.Getenv testing hacks with the build-gated
internal/debug configuration. The access and refresh token lifetime
overrides in internal/config and the verbose refresh logging switch in
the factory now come from GH_INTERNAL_AT_EXPIRES_IN,
GH_INTERNAL_RT_EXPIRES_IN, and GH_INTERNAL_DEBUG_REFRESH_TOKEN, and have
no effect in builds without the ghdebug tag.

Update the refreshable-token e2e scripts to use the new variable names,
rename their own settings to GH_INTERNAL_E2E_BIN, GH_INTERNAL_E2E_HOST,
and GH_INTERNAL_E2E_ALLOW_VSCODE, and refuse to run unless gh version
reports a debug build, pointing at "make debug" otherwise.

commits.messageBody:
script/build skipped rebuilding bin/gh whenever no source file was newer than the binary, regardless of build tags. A plain `make` straight after `make debug` therefore kept the debug binary.

Compare the tags recorded in the existing binary's build info with GO_BUILDTAGS and rebuild when they differ. This also lets `make debug` drop its `rm -f bin/gh` workaround.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: ac178b5a-5b62-49bd-9e83-4796c7ddec46
commits.messageHeadline: chore: rebuild bin/gh when build tags change

commits.messageBody:
Move the environment parsing into an unexported configFromEnv in the untagged config.go. The ghdebug implementation of Config now just calls it, while the release implementation still returns an empty DebugConfig.

This lets the regular test run cover all parsing and panic cases on every OS without the ghdebug tag. The tagged test only checks that Config reads the real environment. Release builds never reference configFromEnv, so the linker still drops the parser and the variable names from them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

The ghdebug implementation of internal/debug is not compiled by the regular test run or build, so it could silently stop compiling. Build ./cmd/gh with the tag on the Ubuntu runner to catch that.
